title: Evaluation of passive control systems for shock wave boundary layer interaction (SWBLI) within a supersonic air inlet
author: Ana Flávia da Silva Tuan

co_advisors.name: André Fernando de Castro da Silva

abstract: This study focuses on RANS simulations in a supersonic inlet with two different systems of passive control: a two-dimensional bump and an air bleed system in the entrance ramp of the inlet. The supersonic inlet serving to capture and decelerate the high-speed incoming flows is aerodynamically indispensable to an airbreathing supersonic aircraft. Sometimes, depending on the conditions of the entry flow, the SWBLI can lead to inlet unstart if not controlled, due to thickened boundary layer. The main goal is to analyze the complex phenomenon of interaction between shock wave and boundary layer and to compare the impact of different methods for the same inlet. Both cases of passive control have been studied, however, their relative efficiencies about each other is still undetermined. With this study, it is possible to determine which passive control system is better depending on the supersonic application.
